ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is the curve of the function f(t), the horizontal axis is t, and the vertical axis is f(t). From the figure, the function values at the left endpoints can be read: when t=0, f(0)=3; when t=2, the curve is on the horizontal axis, so f(2)=0; when t=4, the lowest point is f(4)=-4; when t=6, the point is at -1, so f(6)=-1. Reasoning: The interval [0,8] is divided into 4 subintervals of equal width, and the width is Δt=(8-0)/4=2. Using the left rectangle method, the left endpoints 0,2,4,6 need to be taken. Because the integral is ∫_0^8 |f(t)| dt, take the absolute values: |f(0)|=3, |f(2)|=0, |f(4)|=4, |f(6)|=1. The left rectangle estimate is 2(3+0+4+1)=16.
